## Description

When the browser's terminal writer queue overflows, the terminal halts permanently and nothing repairs it. `SerializedTerminalWriter.degrade('overflow')` sets `halted = true`, drops the queue, and reports `onStreamTruncated`; every later `write()`/`resize()` returns early (`enqueue` checks `halted`). Only `dispose()` clears it, and dispose happens only when the xterm instance is destroyed. A transport reattach reuses the same controller/writer, so a reconnect, a bootstrap, or a new stream all write into a halted writer and are silently dropped.

Found by the #1926 SC-05 100k fixture (PR #2195, run 39708348486): with a 2 s main-thread stall mid-burst, the writer overflowed its old 512-event bound after ~5 000–8 700 displayed lines. The Agent stayed healthy (no subscriber detach, no Server stall verdict), the degraded notice state was set, but the terminal never resumed — the E2E stall detector saw 120 s of no progress on all three attempts.

## Reproduction

1. Attach to a session and start a burst whose chunk count exceeds the writer's event bound while the page's main thread is blocked (PR #2195's 100k fixture does this deterministically).
2. Overflow the writer queue.
3. Observe: the degraded notice appears, but no further output is ever applied; a transport reattach or bootstrap does not resume it.

## Root Cause (verified)

- `web/src/platform/terminal-runtime/controller/SerializedTerminalWriter.ts` — `degrade()` sets `halted = true` and `enqueue()`/`drain()` refuse all later work; only `dispose()` resets `halted`.
- `web/src/platform/terminal-runtime/controller/TerminalController.ts:202-204` — the writer's `onDegraded` only forwards `onStreamTruncated`; it does not rebuild the xterm or replace the writer.
- `SessionRuntime.noteStreamTruncated()` states the gap and requests a bootstrap on the next attach, but the bootstrap is written through the same halted writer.

## Impact

A large burst (or a long main-thread stall during one) leaves the terminal frozen for the rest of the page's life. Recovery requires a page reload; a reconnect cannot repair it. The degraded notice tells the user history is incomplete but not that the terminal will never advance again.

## Fix Direction

Treat writer overflow as a renderer-replacement event at its owner: the controller/runtime must rebuild the xterm (or provide a writer reset gated on a proven baseline) and repaint from a bootstrap, while keeping the degraded state until the repair is proven. A unit test can drive the writer to overflow and assert the controller disposes and replaces it; the 100k E2E (with the stall) is the end-to-end witness.

## Location

- `web/src/platform/terminal-runtime/controller/SerializedTerminalWriter.ts`
- `web/src/platform/terminal-runtime/controller/TerminalController.ts`
- `web/src/platform/session-runtime/SessionRuntime.ts`

### Success Criteria

- [ ] SC-01 A writer overflow disposes/replaces the renderer and repaints from a bootstrap; output resumes without a page reload, and the degraded state clears only on a proven repair.
- [ ] SC-02 A deterministic browser fixture that overflows the writer queue shows the terminal recovering after overflow, not merely displaying a notice.
- [ ] SC-03 Exact PR HEAD Quality/E2E/Case Smoke and merge-SHA trusted Acceptance pass.
